note: HOLDOUT SPEND FREEZE (CLAUDE.md rule 22). A freeze is a SUSPENSION of the authorization that a calibration-complete marker grants, not a withdrawal of the marker itself. TIER-SCOPED since 2026-08-26 (owner ruling, program-director sitting card 6): while `active` is true, no year of a tier named in `scope.tiers` may be solved, scored, or registered for ANY ISO — even with `--holdout-authorized` and that tier's marker present. The current scope is the LOCKED TEST alone (2019, H1-2026, plus every year outside the enumerated tier sets, which scripts/lib/holdout_policy.py fails closed to locked-test): the VALIDATION tier (2020-2022) was lifted from the freeze by the 2026-08-26 ruling and is governed by the `complete` marker + --holdout-authorized alone, exactly as rule 22 specifies (ERCOT/CAISO/MISO hold no `complete` marker and stay refused by the marker gate). The scope is read ONLY by holdout_policy.frozen_tiers, which FAILS CLOSED: an active freeze whose `scope.tiers` is missing, empty, or unparseable covers every tier. The freeze remains deliberately ADDITIVE and backward-compatible: `calibration-complete.json` is untouched by freeze state, so every already-registered out-of-training bundle stays CI-legal and no prior one-shot is invalidated or re-armed. Enforced at the solve entry point by `scripts/run_calibration_full.py::enforce_holdout_year_gate`, which reads this file BEFORE the marker check and fails closed (the replay and knob-jacobian solve paths route through the same gate). Data intake for out-of-training windows is never frozen — and per rule 22 as amended 2026-08-06 ('what is held out is the SCORE, never the DATA or the ARCHITECTURE') intake needs NO authorization at all; the freeze gates only solve/score/registration. [That sentence previously read that intake 'remains permitted under session-logged owner authorization' — the pre-amendment Option-2 regime; corrected 2026-08-26 with the scope edit.] Changing the freeze's scope or lifting it is an owner action recorded in `history` with the reason; no session changes it by inference.

reason: The CAMPD unit-outage detector books sustained economic layup as mechanical outage in ALL SIX ISO extracts (neiso-63, 2026-07-24; evidence results/calibration/FINDING-neiso63-campd-economic-layup-2026-07.md). Every ISO books 23-46% of its CC capacity-year as outage against a real EFOR+planned norm of ~10-15%. The availability envelope every keeper is calibrated against is therefore about to change materially. A validation or locked-test year scored now would be measuring the wrong fleet: a MISS would be uninterpretable (detector defect or genuine forecast error?) and a PASS would be actively misleading, because the locked tier is touch-once and cannot be re-scored after the fix lands. Freezing preserves the out-of-sample years as usable evidence instead of spending them on a known-defective input.
lifts_when: The remaining LOCKED-TEST freeze lifts only by a further explicit owner action recorded here — there is no standing condition that lifts it, and granting an ISO a `final` marker does NOT lift it (the freeze outranks the marker and is checked first). Related standing precondition for any future `final` grant (owner ruling 2026-08-26, card 7): an ISO becomes eligible to be CONSIDERED for `final` only after its 2020-2022 validation touchpoints have been run and the touchpoint loop has stopped surfacing repairs; eligibility is not a grant — `final` remains an explicit owner act, per ISO, every time. [The original `lifts_when`, whose close-with-cause branch the 2026-08-26 card-6 ruling took, is preserved verbatim in that ruling's history entry.]

history.reason: The charter (docs/handoffs/campd-economic-layup-fix-charter-2026-07.md) is CLOSED WITH CAUSE in the same ruling (its §10), and the cause is stated rather than implied: the CAMPD economic-layup detector question REMAINS OPEN — the post-guard CC_REGULAR outage share is 14.2-36.7% with 17 of 18 ISO-years above the ~10-15% EFOR+planned norm (audit row O4 re-measurement, 2026-08-18), and charter §9 records the residual as a definitional seam (published series measure unavailability; the CEMS detector measures non-operation) that four independent investigation lanes showed is NOT closable by any admissible discriminator. The lift is therefore a decision to proceed WITH a known-open input question, carried explicitly as a documented seam that every keeper's availability envelope inherits — NOT a finding that the question closed. The asymmetry that justifies the scope is the one the owner relied on in both prior narrow lifts: validation years (2020-2022) are ITERABLE, re-spendable, model-selection-only evidence, so spending one against an imperfect envelope costs nothing irreversible and re-opens the diagnostic touchpoint loop (rule 22) that has already surfaced two real input defects (neiso-85/86 inverted gas basis); locked-test years (2019, H1-2026) are touch-once and STAY FROZEN for every ISO. This is a STANDING re-scope, not a lift/spend/re-arm cycle: the steady state is now an active freeze over the locked tier only, expressed as scope.tiers = ['locked_test'] with active still true, enforced by the fail-closed holdout_policy.frozen_tiers reader. The file's `lifts_when` at the time of this ruling read, verbatim: 'The merit-order-guard fix charter (docs/handoffs/campd-economic-layup-fix-charter-2026-07.md) reaches a decision — either the corrected detector is adopted and each affected ISO's keeper is re-audited on the corrected envelope, or the charter is closed with cause and the extract is confirmed fit for purpose. The owner lifts the freeze explicitly; no session lifts it by inference from a passing metric.' Its close-with-cause branch is taken WITHOUT the 'extract is confirmed fit for purpose' clause being met as written — what is confirmed is that the extract is the best BUILDABLE representation (the four negative lanes), which is a weaker and honestly different statement.
